newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan finance, welfare ministries agree on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Japan finance, welfare ministries agree on rate cut.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced on Friday that it will cut the interest rate paid on the deposits it holds for other ministries by 0.1 percentage point to 2.8 percent, effective from March 19.
The cut came after the MOF and the Health and Welfare Ministry set aside a dispute over the cut and reached an agreement on Thursday evening.
The ministry said the interest rate cut on deposits at its Trust Fund Bureau will take effect from March 19.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday that Health and Welfare Minister Junichiro Koizumi agreed to the cut after a discussion on Thursday evening.

MOF had been pushing to cut the rate which has remained unchanged at a record low 2.9 percent since January despite a recent fall in the 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) coupon rate, on which the deposit rate is customarily set.

The Trust Fund Bureau channels funds raised via deposits made by the Health and Posts and Telecommunications ministries to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-government bodies for the fiscal investment and loan programme (FILP).
The cut had been delayed as Koizumi, a fierce opponent of FILP, refused to accept it.
Koizumi has said that FILP should either be stopped or revamped because the quasi-governmental financial institutions and bodies are inefficiently managed.
The cut will give these institutions greater room to invest, but the impact on the bond market is likely to be limited, said Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities Co Ltd.
"As the market interest rates have already fallen below (the deposit rate) long ago, the cut is unlikely to result in a big change in their investment activity," he said
The yield of the benchmark 10-year JGB has been falling sharply recently. It fell to a record low of 2.190 percent on Friday afternoon.
